probes.notes: MKM: GBM logloss trivially better (0.6664 < 0.6665) but GBM AUC trivially worse (0.6154 < 0.6156). Logloss and AUC optimise different things (calibration vs rank order); the direction inconsistency is 1e-4-level noise, not contradictory.

old_80k_dsk_baseline.notes: Old sample-based run from game-data-value-model.md Step 2 / synergy-probe.md. At 80k scale GBM was actually WORSE than linear (0.671 > 0.668); full-data confirms this was small-data noise, not a win.

verifier_verdict: CONFIRMED-LINEAR. Three reasons: (a) cross-set consistency at 10x scale with magnitude zero — GBM beats linear by at most 0.0001 logloss, pair deltas symmetric noise in {-0.0001, 0, +0.0001}; (b) n_games match the WS1.1 build table exactly and AUC/logloss directions are internally consistent (the MKM inconsistency is 1e-4-level calibration-vs-rank noise); (c) MKM is the hardest case — a Detective-synergy set where face-plausible combos are detected yet add +0.0000 held-out.

caveats.summary: GBM architecturally capped relative to full data
caveats.detail: The GBM is HistGradientBoostingClassifier with max_iter=300, max_leaf_nodes=31, early_stopping=True (default n_iter_no_change=10). At 800k training rows the same cap is far more constraining relative to data than at 64k. A skeptic could argue the GBM should have been scaled up with the data; a deeper/longer-budget GBM arm would make the bound airtight. Counter-point: early_stopping means the GBM stops when its internal validation (~80k rows) stops improving — if the linear model exhausts the signal at that scale, the budget question is moot.

caveats.summary: pair-selection --min-support 150 was NOT scaled with the data
caveats.detail: At ~1M games, min-support=150 is ~0.023% of games (vs ~0.23% at 80k games). This admits ~4,001–4,005 candidate pairs — far more than at the old scale — potentially including noisier low-support pairs. The held-out test still catching nothing is reassuring, but a min-support~1500 re-run (matching the old ~0.23% threshold) would be the cleaner test. Does not affect the aggregate logloss result, only individual pair rankings.

implication: Linearity holds at ~10x data across three formats with different synergy themes (horror-tribal, gift/boon, detective). Pool-conditioned pick objectives stay dead. WS3 (replay-data credit assignment) is the only remaining route to a richer outcome signal.
